words.gloss: like the enemy of clay (the tool that cuts it)

literal: Fearing internal enmity, protect oneself; at the time of weakness, like the enemy of clay, it will destroy completely.
translation: One must fear internal enmity and guard oneself against it; otherwise, at a moment of weakness, it will destroy one completely, just as a tool cuts through clay.
modern: உட்பகைக்கு அஞ்சி ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்; இல்லையெனில், தளர்ச்சி ஏற்படும் காலத்தில், அது மண்ணை அறுக்கும் கருவியைப் போல அவனை முற்றிலும் அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the extreme danger of internal enmity, which refers to hostility from those within one's own circle. The poet advises that one must fear and guard against such hidden enemies constantly. If left unchecked, at the first sign of vulnerability or distress, this internal enemy will destroy a person completely. The destruction is compared to the tool that cuts clay, which slices through soft clay effortlessly and decisively.
